summary.title: Space Invaders from Scratch - Part 3
summary.one_liner: You learn how to add a player and an alien swarm to a C++ Space Invaders clone, animate sprites by frame counting, and use V-sync to tie animation timing to game cycles.
keywords: how to animate sprites in a game
takeaways: Model the player, aliens and overall game state as C++ structs with pixel positions and lives.
Store sprites as 1-bit bitmaps and draw them into a pixel buffer each frame.
Animate sprites by cycling through a SpriteAnimation array of frames, measured in game loop iterations.
Use glfwSwapInterval(1) (V-sync) to fix the frame rate at the monitor refresh rate, so animation timing is in cycles.
Keep the player inside screen bounds with simple edge checks that reverse movement direction.
summary.summary: The post continues the Space Invaders clone in C++ with minimal dependencies (GLFW for windowing). It introduces Alien, Player and Game structs, defines the player and alien sprites as bitmaps, and lays out 55 aliens in a grid as in the original arcade game. It then adds a SpriteAnimation struct that cycles two alien frames, counting time in loop iterations, and relies on V-sync to make that timing consistent. A simple back-and-forth player movement with bounds checks completes the demo, and the next part covers keyboard input.
